content.title: WNBA draft results 2026: Wings select Azzi Fudd No. 1, Olivia Miles goes No. 2 to Lynx, Flau'jae Johnson's draft rights traded
content.text: The 2026 WNBA Draft has come and gone, kicking off the league’s 30th anniversary season.For the second consecutive year, the Dallas Wings held the No. 1 overall pick, and they decided to reunite UConn stars Paige Bueckers and Azzi Fudd as they look to build a contender. Fudd will be making a record-setting $500,000 in her first season, fresh off a new collective bargaining agreement between the league and WNBPA that has increased the WNBA’s salary cap to $7 million in 2026, up from just over $1.5 million last season.AdvertisementTCU’s Olivia Miles went No. 2 to the Minnesota Lynx, Spain’s Awa Fam Thiam went third to the Seattle Storm, UCLA’s Lauren Betts went fourth to the Washington Mystics and Betts’ teammate Gabriela Jaquez went fifth to the Chicago Sky to round out the top five.The champion Bruins had a record-setting night with six players drafted, while the big surprise was the trade of Flau’jae Johnson’s draft rights from the Golden State Valkyries to the Seattle Storm.First round resultsNo. 1: Azzi Fudd, Dallas Wings No. 2: Olivia Miles, its first national championship, UCLA women’s basketball is setting records in the WNBA.The Bruins had six players selected in Monday’s WNBA Draft, the most ever by one school in a single draft. Five went in the first round, which was also a WNBA Draft record.Two-time All-American and Final Four MOP Lauren Betts was the first Bruin off the board at No. 4 to the Washington Mystics. Betts’ selection started a run of three straight Bruins picks. Her UCLA teammate Angela Dugalić then joined her on the Mystics at No. 9.Gianna Kneepkens and Charlisse Leger-Walker will also be teammates on the Connecticut Sun.No. 4: Lauren Betts, Washington Mystics No. 5: Gabriela Jaquez, Chicago Sky No. 6: Kiki Rice, Toronto Tempo No. 9: Angela Dugalić, Washington Mystics No. 15: Gianna Kneepkens, Connecticut Sun No. 18: Charlisse Leger-Walker, Connecticut SunFour teams previously had five total players selected in the same draft: 2023 South Carolina, 2019 Notre Dame and Tennessee twice (1999 and 2008).Read more here.Tue, April 14, 2026 at 1:01 AM UTCYahoo Sports StaffWith the 27th pick, the Mercury select Ines Pitarch-Granel, and the Dream select Indya Nivar with the 28th pick.Tue, April 14, 2026 at 12:51 AM UTCYahoo Sports StaffWith the 20th overall pick, the L.A.
